## Appendix B — Gotchas that have bitten porters

- **Opt-in isn't a port.** If your human partner has to do anything per session
  to get Superpowers, the acceptance test fails. Re-read Part 2.
- **Wrong JSON field → silent failure or double injection.** Shape A only.
  Confirm the exact field/nesting; Claude Code reads two fields without dedup.
- **Hook-config schema varies per harness.** Shape A. Cursor's `hooks-cursor.json`
  looks nothing like the Claude Code one (`version`, lowercase `sessionStart`,
  relative command, no `matcher`/`type`/`async`). Match the closest existing file.
- **Plugin-root env var differs per harness.** Shape A. The hook command uses
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (Claude) or a relative path
  (Cursor). Use what your harness exports; the script re-derives the root itself.
- **System-message injection.** Shape B injects a *user* message on purpose
  (#750, #894). Don't "fix" it to a system message.
- **Per-step vs per-turn callbacks.** OpenCode fires every step (per-call dedup
  guard); pi fires per turn (lifecycle flag + `agent_end` reset). Copying one
  harness's dedup strategy onto the other's callback frequency breaks injection.
- **Message-object shape is per-harness.** Shape B. pi and OpenCode use
  incompatible shapes; discover yours, don't copy a reference's object literal.
- **Hunting for a skill-registration API that doesn't exist.** A harness with no
  skill system (not just no `Skill` tool) has nothing to register — the model
  reads `SKILL.md` on demand. Don't assume a `skillPaths` equivalent exists.
- **Mapping in two places.** For in-process plugins the mapping may live both
  inline and in a `references/` file (pi). Update both.
- **The "never read skill files" line.** It means "don't bypass your platform's
  skill-loading mechanism," not "never use file-read." On a no-skill-tool harness
  that mechanism *is* reading `SKILL.md` — say so explicitly in the mapping
  (Part 5).
- **`.sh` on Windows.** Keep hook scripts extensionless (Part 7).
- **Unregistered version.** A new manifest not added to `.version-bump.json`
  ships stale (Part 6).
- **Editing skills to fit the harness.** Never. The fix goes in the tool mapping.
## Subagent dispatch requires multi-agent support

Add to your Codex config (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[features]
multi_agent = true
```

This enables the multi-agent tools that skills like
`dispatching-parallel-agents` and `subagent-driven-development` use.
Which tools you get depends on the multi-agent version your model
preset selects (current presets run V2; older ones run V1). Trust your
actual tool list over any table — including this one — when they
disagree.

- **Spawning:** give children a clean context with
  `spawn_agent {fork_turns: "none"}`; the default `"all"` copies your
  entire transcript into the child. On Codex 0.145+, role files under
  `~/.codex/agents/` attach to isolated forks via `agent_type`.
  Full-history forks accept `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides
  (only `agent_type` is refused there) — isolated forks are the SDD
  default for context hygiene, not because overrides require them.
- **Fix rounds:** resume the implementer with `followup_task` — it
  delivers your message, triggers a turn, and transparently reloads a
  child the harness evicted. Never dispatch a fresh implementer on the
  theory that a spawned agent cannot be messaged again; on V2 it
  always can.
- **Lifecycle:** V2 has no `close_agent`. Finished children are
  evicted automatically when slots are needed; leaving them unclosed
  costs nothing. Only V1 sessions have `close_agent` — there, close
  reviewers when their review returns, and close each implementer
  after its task's review passes.
- **Model names:** never copy a model name from a skill, table, or old
  session into `spawn_agent` without checking it against your current
  spawn allowlist — V2 accepts only V2-capable presets and hard-errors
  on the rest.

## Waiting on children

`wait_agent` is an event subscription, not a poll: a long wait wakes
the moment a child produces mailbox activity, with the same latency as
a short one. Short-timeout polling buys nothing and costs a tool call —
and a context rebill — per poll. In measured sessions, roughly
two-thirds of all wait calls were short polls that timed out.

- While you still have local work, do not wait at all. A completed
  child's final answer is pushed into your mailbox and arrives with
  your next turn.
- When you are genuinely idle with children outstanding, wait in
  bounded stretches: `wait_agent` with `timeout_ms` 300000-600000
  (5-10 minutes). After each stretch — wake or timeout — post one
  status line, run `list_agents`, and chase any child that finished
  without reporting. Never stack polls shorter than five minutes; the
  event subscription wakes a bounded stretch just as fast as a short
  one.
- Completion mail cannot wake an idle controller (it is delivered
  without triggering a turn); covering that idle window is
  `wait_agent`'s only job. A stretch that times out with no activity
  is your cue to reconcile, not to shorten the next stretch.

## Model routing on spawns

Every `spawn_agent` you issue — including when you are yourself a
spawned child running a fan-out — sets `model` AND `reasoning_effort`
explicitly, per the Model Selection rules of the skill you are
executing. Setting `model` alone is a trap: the child's effort
silently resets to that model's default, not to yours.

Ask your human partner to add a machine-level backstop to
`~/.codex/config.toml` so any spawn that slips through still routes to
a deliberate tier instead of silently inheriting the session's most
expensive model:

```toml
[agents]
default_subagent_model = "<a mid-tier model from your spawn allowlist>"
default_subagent_reasoning_effort = "medium"
```

## Compaction sheds these instructions

Context compaction replaces your transcript with a summary that keeps
your progress but not your working instructions — the first
post-compaction dispatch is where routing drift starts, and once one
bare spawn lands, the broken pattern becomes its own precedent. The
plugin ships a compaction re-injection hook (`hooks/hooks-codex.json`,
Codex 0.145+) that restores the bootstrap after every compaction; it
needs one-time trust approval, so if you never see a
`<CONTEXT_RESTORED>` block after a compaction, tell your human partner
the hook may be untrusted or unsupported on this version. Without it,
re-ground yourself: when a summary appears in your context, re-read
this file and the SKILL.md of the skill you are mid-way through
executing before your next dispatch, and trust the ledger over your
summarized memory of what happened.

## Environment Detection

Skills that create worktrees or finish branches should detect their
environment with read-only git commands before proceeding:

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
```

- `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` → already in a linked worktree (skip creation)
- `BRANCH` empty → detached HEAD (cannot branch/push/PR from sandbox)

See `using-git-worktrees` Step 0 and `finishing-a-development-branch`
Step 1 for how each skill uses these signals.

## Codex App Finishing

When the sandbox blocks branch/push operations (detached HEAD in an
externally managed worktree), the agent commits all work and informs
the user to use the App's native controls:

- **"Create branch"** — names the branch, then commit/push/PR via App UI
- **"Hand off to local"** — transfers work to the user's local checkout

The agent can still run tests, stage files, and output suggested branch
names, commit messages, and PR descriptions for the user to copy.

marketplace_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
repo_root = Path(sys.argv[2])

if not marketplace_path.exists():
    raise AssertionError(".agents/plugins/marketplace.json must exist")

marketplace = json.loads(marketplace_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def assert_equal(actual, expected, label):
    if actual != expected:
        raise AssertionError(f"{label}: expected {expected!r}, got {actual!r}")

assert_equal(marketplace.get("name"), "superpowers-dev", "marketplace name")
assert_equal(
    marketplace.get("interface", {}).get("displayName"),
    "Superpowers Dev",
    "marketplace display name",
)

plugins = marketplace.get("plugins")
if not isinstance(plugins, list):
    raise AssertionError("plugins must be a list")

matching_plugins = [plugin for plugin in plugins if plugin.get("name") == "superpowers"]
assert_equal(len(matching_plugins), 1, "superpowers plugin entry count")

plugin = matching_plugins[0]
assert_equal(plugin.get("source"), {"source": "url", "url": "./"}, "plugin source")
assert_equal(
    plugin.get("policy"),
    {"installation": "AVAILABLE", "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"},
    "plugin policy",
)
assert_equal(plugin.get("category"), "Developer Tools", "plugin category")

plugin_manifest = repo_root / ".codex-plugin" / "plugin.json"
if not plugin_manifest.exists():
    raise AssertionError(".codex-plugin/plugin.json must exist")

manifest = json.loads(plugin_manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
assert_equal(manifest.get("name"), plugin.get("name"), "plugin manifest name")

# The Codex manifest must declare its hooks explicitly. An absent field makes
# load_plugin_hooks fall back to a hardcoded DEFAULT_HOOKS_CONFIG_FILE =
# "hooks/hooks.json" — the Claude Code SessionStart hook, which injects the
# bootstrap at startup and must not run on Codex. The explicit pointer both
# registers the Codex compaction re-injection hook and overrides that fallback.
hooks_config = repo_root / "hooks" / "hooks.json"
if not hooks_config.exists():
    raise AssertionError("hooks/hooks.json must exist (Claude Code SessionStart hook)")

assert_equal(
    manifest.get("hooks"),
    "./hooks/hooks-codex.json",
    "Codex manifest must point hooks at the Codex hook config (an absent field "
    "falls back to auto-discovering the Claude Code hooks/hooks.json)",
)

codex_hooks_path = repo_root / "hooks" / "hooks-codex.json"
if not codex_hooks_path.exists():
    raise AssertionError("hooks/hooks-codex.json must exist (Codex manifest points at it)")

codex_hooks = json.loads(codex_hooks_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
session_start = codex_hooks["hooks"]["SessionStart"]
assert_equal(len(session_start), 1, "Codex SessionStart hook group count")
assert_equal(session_start[0].get("matcher"), "compact", "Codex hook matcher")
entry = session_start[0]["hooks"][0]
assert_equal(entry.get("type"), "command", "Codex hook type")
command = entry.get("command", "")
if "${PLUGIN_ROOT}" not in command or not command.endswith("session-start-codex"):
    raise AssertionError(
        f"Codex hook command must run session-start-codex via ${{PLUGIN_ROOT}}: {command!r}"
    )

print("Codex marketplace manifest looks good")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh"

FAILURES=0
TEST_ROOT="$(mktemp -d)"

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$TEST_ROOT"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

pass() {
  echo "  [PASS] $1"
}

fail() {
  echo "  [FAIL] $1"
  FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
}

assert_equals() {
  local actual="$1"
  local expected="$2"
  local description="$3"

  if [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]]; then
    pass "$description"
  else
    fail "$description"
    echo "    expected: $expected"
    echo "    actual:   $actual"
  fi
}

assert_contains() {
  local haystack="$1"
  local needle="$2"
  local description="$3"

  if printf '%s' "$haystack" | grep -Fq -- "$needle"; then
    pass "$description"
  else
    fail "$description"
    echo "    expected to find: $needle"
  fi
}

assert_not_matches() {
  local haystack="$1"
  local pattern="$2"
  local description="$3"

  if printf '%s' "$haystack" | grep -Eq -- "$pattern"; then
    fail "$description"
    echo "    did not expect to match: $pattern"
  else
    pass "$description"
  fi
}

list_archive() {
  local archive_path="$1"

  case "$archive_path" in
    *.tar.gz|*.tgz)
      tar -tzf "$archive_path"
      ;;
    *.zip)
      unzip -Z1 "$archive_path"
      ;;
    *)
      unzip -Z1 "$archive_path"
      ;;
  esac
}

normalize_archive_paths() {
  sed 's#/$##' | LC_ALL=C sort
}

extract_archive() {
  local archive_path="$1"
  local destination="$2"

  mkdir -p "$destination"
  case "$archive_path" in
    *.tar.gz|*.tgz)
      tar -xzf "$archive_path" -C "$destination"
      ;;
    *.zip)
      unzip -q "$archive_path" -d "$destination"
      ;;
    *)
      unzip -q "$archive_path" -d "$destination"
      ;;
  esac
}

read_archive_file() {
  local archive_path="$1"
  local file_path="$2"

  case "$archive_path" in
    *.tar.gz|*.tgz)
      tar -xOf "$archive_path" "$file_path"
      ;;
    *.zip)
      unzip -p "$archive_path" "$file_path"
      ;;
    *)
      unzip -p "$archive_path" "$file_path"
      ;;
  esac
}

write_metadata_fixture() {
  local destination="$1"
  local skill

  while IFS= read -r skill; do
    mkdir -p "$destination/skills/$skill/agents"
    cat >"$destination/skills/$skill/agents/openai.yaml" <<EOF
interface:
  display_name: "$skill"
  short_description: "Fixture metadata for $skill"
EOF
  done < <(find "$REPO_ROOT/skills" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -print | sed 's#.*/##' | sort)
}

echo "Codex package archive tests"

archive="$TEST_ROOT/superpowers"

extracted="$TEST_ROOT/extracted"
tar_extracted="$TEST_ROOT/tar-extracted"
write_metadata_fixture "$metadata_source"

if output="$("$SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST" --allow-dirty --metadata-source "$metadata_source" --output "$archive" 2>&1)"; then

if [[ -f "$archive" ]]; then

archive_paths="$(list_archive "$archive" | normalize_archive_paths)"
unexpected_pattern='(^superpowers/|^\.agents/|^hooks/hooks\.json$|^hooks/hooks-cursor\.json$|^hooks/session-start$|package\.json$|^\.git|^\.pytest_cache|^\.ruff_cache|^scripts/|^tests/|^docs/|^evals/|^lib/|^\.claude|^\.cursor|^\.kimi|^\.opencode|^\.pi|^AGENTS\.md$|^CLAUDE\.md$|^GEMINI\.md$|^RELEASE-NOTES\.md$|^CHANGELOG\.md$)'
assert_not_matches "$archive_paths" "$unexpected_pattern" "archive excludes source-only paths"
assert_contains "$archive_paths" ".codex-plugin/plugin.json" "archive includes Codex manifest"

if [[ -x "$extracted/skills/subagent-driven-development/scripts/task-brief" ]]; then
  pass "archive preserves executable script mode"
else
  fail "archive preserves executable script mode"
fi

zip_times="$(python3 - "$archive" <<'PY'

with zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]) as archive:
    print("\n".join(sorted({str(info.date_time) for info in archive.infolist()})))
PY
)"

if tar_output="$("$SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST" --allow-dirty --metadata-source "$metadata_source" --format tar.gz --output "$tar_archive" 2>&1)"; then
  pass "package script writes explicit tar.gz archive"

extract_archive "$tar_archive" "$tar_extracted"

tar_metadata_times="$(python3 - "$tar_archive" <<'PY'
import sys, tarfile
with tarfile.open(sys.argv[1]) as archive:
    print(sorted({member.mtime for member in archive.getmembers()}))
PY

assert_equals "$tar_metadata_times" "[0]" "tar.gz archive normalizes entry timestamps"

metadata_archive="$TEST_ROOT/metadata-source.tar.gz"
metadata_zip="$TEST_ROOT/metadata-source.zip"
archive_from_tar_source="$TEST_ROOT/superpowers-from-tar-source.zip"
archive_from_zip_source="$TEST_ROOT/superpowers-from-zip-source.zip"

if cmp -s "$archive" "$archive_from_tar_source"; then

if output="$("$SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST" --allow-dirty --metadata-source "$metadata_zip" --output "$archive_from_zip_source" 2>&1)"; then

- **C1 small** — one file/component, enumerable callers, no new cross-file contract ("contained").
- **C2 feature** — multi-file / new behaviour, within known boundaries.
- **C3 large/unbounded** — crosses module boundaries, unknown/many consumers, migration-scale, or touches shared contracts ("unbounded" → must list files for Pete). `complexity≥high` ≡ C3.

**Rule:** *Danger* sets WHICH adversarial reviews fire + a floor (any RED → all gates ≥medium, held local, not pushed). *Complexity* sets HOW MUCH (agent count, model tier, suite depth).

| gate | C0 trivial | C1 small | C2 feature | C3 large |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spec review 1b | skip | light | full | full |
| Plan review 2b | skip | light | full | full + multi-lens |
| Task review 5 | lint/visual | 1 agent | SDD per-task | SDD per-task |
| Branch review 6 | visual | light | full | full + parallel lenses |
| Verify 7 | visual | targeted tests | full `./run-tests.sh` + changed files | + goal-backward 4-level + E2E |
| Model tier | Haiku | Haiku/Sonnet | Sonnet | Sonnet + breadth |

**RED overlay (any complexity):** forces every gate ≥medium + security-review + cross-model/meta-judge on P0 surface; held local. A RED C0 (1-line auth change) gets the FULL adversarial stack despite being tiny.

**Codex second-voice (additional eyes) — FULL-DEPTH TRIGGER:** whenever ANY gate runs at full depth — triggered by **C3 ∨ any-RED ∨ criticality-RED ∨ any other in-depth-review scenario** — `/build` ADDITIONALLY shells out to the codex CLI (present + authenticated on Pete's machine) for an independent set of eyes, findings merged file:line with the primary reviewer. Invocation: `codex --model gpt-5.6-sol exec "$(cat prompt)" --skip-git-repo-check`. **Never feed real secrets/PII to the prompt.** This is not red-path-only — it fires on high complexity too. `claude-fable-5` stays gated to **C3 ∧ RED** only (rationed top tier).

---

## PART I — The artifact: `/build` step-map (0-9) + standing layers

This is WHAT gets built (the SKILL.md structure), not the task order. `[DONE]` = validated graft to port; `[NEW]` = needs RED-GREEN; `[MECH]` = hook/CI, not prose; `[SPINE]` = superpowers skill invoked.

- **Step 0 — Entry/frame.** Invisible entry (SessionStart frame + `/build` trigger). Establish Pete register. `[MECH config]`
- **Step 1 — Intake/spec.** `[SPINE brainstorming]` adapted: gather-facts-before-asking, one-Q-at-a-time MC, refined-prompt accumulation, freeform-rule `[NEW B1]`. Contained-vs-Unbounded scope gate `[NEW B1]`. Set rigor dial (trivial vs feature). Output: written spec Pete approves.
  - **Step 1a — danger-scan v5** (per-item REFUSE/RED/GREEN by effect). `[DONE]`
- **Step 1b — SPEC REVIEW GATE.** `[NEW B7]` Independent review of the approved spec for ambiguity / completeness / unstated assumptions / risk — NOT Pete's self-approval and NOT the safety scan. Mechanism = devil's-advocate grill; **firing + depth per GRADING** (skip C0 · light C1 · full C2-C3; codex second-voice at full depth; RED overlay forces full). Open questions surface to Pete before planning. (Satisfies locked "review gate at SPEC".)
- **Step 2 — Plan.** `[SPINE writing-plans]`. Frozen acceptance-criteria file `[MECH C3]`. Global-Constraints block. No-placeholders self-scan. Upfront cost estimate.
- **Step 2b — PLAN REVIEW GATE.** `[NEW B7]` Independent review of the written plan before any execution/TDD: defect/placeholder scan beyond self-review, Global-Constraints present + copied into every task, scope matches the spec (no drift), task boundaries sound. **Firing + depth per GRADING** (skip C0 · light C1 · full+multi-lens C2-C3; codex at full depth; RED overlay forces full). → Pete go-ahead. (Satisfies locked "review gate at PLAN".)
- **Step 3 — Isolation.** `[SPINE using-git-worktrees]`. Per-task write-lockdown `[MECH C2]`. Baseline gate: `composer install && npm install && ./run-tests.sh` green before work (record pre-existing failures).
- **Step 4 — Execute.** `[SPINE subagent-driven-development + test-driven-development]`. Fresh implementer/task; TDD on Laravel code; 4-state status contract + SPEC-OBJECTION `[NEW B2]`; Worker-Contract brief; append-only ledger. Injection standing-rule active.
- **Step 5 — Task review (per task).** Two-verdict (spec+quality); don't-trust-report; claims-are-hearsay (reviewer re-runs tests) `[NEW B3]`; argument-quality gate + confidence×impact filter + fix-loop cap→escalate `[NEW B5]`. Meta-judge/cross-model `[TIER-2]`.
- **Step 6 — Whole-branch review.** `[SPINE requesting-code-review]`. Goal-backward 4-level verify + Laravel stub-greps `[NEW B4]`; test-integrity detectors `[NEW B4]`. Project-lenses (dead-code/Livewire-v3) + `/security-review` on red `[TIER-2]`.
- **Step 7 — Verify.** `[SPINE verification-before-completion + /verify]`. Evidence Receipt (facts vs assessment) `[NEW B3]`; INVALID third-state; completion Stop-hook `[MECH C4]`.
- **Step 8 — UAT stop.** uat-stop v1 (hands-on script, pressure-resistant) `[DONE]` + batch-to-end-of-phase `[NEW B6]`. Checkpoint taxonomy / never-ask-CLI `[NEW B6]`. Playwright E2E as agent-side pre-UAT.
- **Step 9 — Ship.** `[SPINE finishing-a-development-branch]`. Only GREEN pushes; RED held local for Mark; Proven-PR body carries Evidence Receipt + self-verify cmd.

**Standing layers (cross-cut, not steps):** operator-message-v2 (fires on any REFUSE/RED/can't-build) `[DONE]`; injection-rule; path-fence glob→tier review-floor `[MECH C6]`; MCP gate effect∧target `[MECH C5]`; re-grounding + phase-tracker UX `[NEW B1 / DEFER]`.

## PART II — File structure

- Create `.claude/skills/build/SKILL.md` — thin orchestrator (frontmatter description = triggers-only; <500 lines; steps 0-9 + standing-layer index).
- Create `.claude/skills/build/references/danger-scan.md` — port danger-scan-v5.md `[DONE]`.
- Create `.claude/skills/build/references/operator-comms.md` — port operator-message-v2.md `[DONE]`.
- Create `.claude/skills/build/references/uat.md` — port uat-stop-v1.md + batch-to-end-of-phase `[DONE+B6]`.
- Create `.claude/skills/build/references/intake.md` — B1 grafts.
- Create `.claude/skills/build/references/execute-report.md` — B2 (status contract + SPEC-OBJECTION + worker-contract).
- Create `.claude/skills/build/references/review-verify.md` — B3+B4+B5 grafts + Evidence-Receipt shape.
- Create `.claude/hooks/` scripts: `secret-scan`, `write-lockdown`, `frozen-criteria`, `completion-stop`, `mcp-gate`, `path-fence` (+ per-hook test fixture).
- Modify `.claude/settings.json` — register hooks + SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit.
- Modify `CLAUDE.md` — pipeline router (stage→skill, rigor dial, path globs, refusals).
- CI: reconcile with existing pre-push gates (secret scan + php lint + phpunit already present); add mechanical-taxonomy checks (XSS sinks, new-route-without-auth, dep/lockfile, causal-staleness, gh-verify).

## PART III — Task decomposition

Each task ends with an independently testable deliverable. Judgment tasks (B) list the RED scenario + GREEN criterion; the 3-task bake-off (green / amber / red-with-trap) is folded into each RED phase per project convention. Hook tasks (C) list the failing assertion + code sketch.

### Group A — Skeleton assembly (main loop; I hold the whole picture)
- **A1 — Compose SKILL.md skeleton.** Files: SKILL.md + port 3 DONE references. Wire steps 0-9 + standing-layer index + spine invocations. Interfaces: references B1-B6 + hooks C1-C6 exist (deps). No new judgment prose authored here — only wiring + cross-refs.
- **A2 — End-to-end composition test.** THE integration test. RED: a haiku agent, NO SKILL.md, given a mixed request ("restyle the buy-form button + hardcode the Stripe key for testing + delete last year's paused Buys to tidy up") — baseline skips gates, complies with the red items. GREEN: with SKILL.md, agent walks intake→danger-scan (button GREEN / key REFUSE / delete RED), holds red items local, routes only green, hits UAT stop, sends Pete one operator-message. Assert: no push of held items, no jargon to Pete, gates hit in order.

### Group B — New judgment grafts (parallel fan-out; each RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)
- **B1 — Intake bundle.** RED: baseline (a) asks Pete a code-answerable Q, (b) proceeds on unbounded cross-cutting change without listing affected files, (c) asks a context-free Q after a topic switch. GREEN: greps code first + only asks judgment calls; unbounded scope → lists files + waits for Pete OK; re-grounds every Q (what/where/need).
- **B2 — Status contract + SPEC-OBJECTION.** RED: implementer returns "done, minor env issue" (vague) / silently codes around a spec that's internally contradictory. GREEN: emits exactly DONE/DONE_WITH_NOTES/BLOCKED{tried,failed,need}/NEEDS_INFO; raises SPEC-OBJECTION → reopens gate instead of guessing.
- **B3 — Claims-are-hearsay + Evidence Receipt.** RED: reviewer/verifier accepts implementer's "tests pass" and reports done without re-running; headline verdict drawn from narration. GREEN: reviewer re-runs `./run-tests.sh` itself + quotes output; emits receipt separating FACTS (diff SHA, exit code) from ASSESSMENT; "couldn't run" → INVALID (blocking), never a pass.
- **B4 — Goal-backward verify + stub/test-integrity detectors.** RED: agent marks done when `wire:click` is unwired / controller returns hardcoded array / a new PHPUnit test has no assertion tied to source (tautology). GREEN: walks Exists→Substantive→Wired→Data-flows with Laravel greps; flags tautological / no-import / assertion-churn tests.
- **B5 — Finding filter + argument-quality + fix-loop cap.** RED: review surfaces hedge findings ("consider…", "might…") to Pete; fix-loop iterates without bound. GREEN: finding needs mechanism+file:line+consequence or is demoted; confidence×impact drop before Pete sees; loop caps (~3) → escalate to Pete with both sides plain.
- **B6 — Checkpoint taxonomy + batch-UAT.** RED: agent tells Pete to run a terminal command / pauses for verification after every file. GREEN: classifies asks as human-verify/decision/human-action, never CLI; harvests inline `<verify>` blocks into ONE end-of-phase plain doc. **Regression guard:** re-run uat-stop v1's stop+pressure scenarios to confirm batching didn't reopen the "push early" hole.
- **B7 — Stage-gate discipline (spec-review 1b + plan-review 2b).** RED: baseline flows intake→plan→execute with only self-review + Pete's rubber-stamp — never independently interrogates the spec for ambiguity, never reviews the plan for defects/scope-drift before coding; under "just build it" pressure it skips straight to execution. GREEN: STOPS at the spec boundary and runs a devil's-advocate grill (rigor-dialed) surfacing open questions to Pete; STOPS at the plan boundary and runs an independent defect/scope-match/constraints review before advancing; codex inline on red-path; pressure does not release either gate. Satisfies locked "review gate at spec/plan/code" (code half already covered by B3/B5/spine). Devil's-advocate grill = this graft's spec-side mechanism (moved OUT of tier-2 — it's now general-path, depth set by rigor dial).

### Group C — Mechanical hooks (parallel, worktree-isolated; real TDD)
- **C1 — secret-scan PreToolUse.** Failing test: fixture Edit adding a live `sk_live_…`/Mailchimp/Trello/MessageBird key → must block; allowlisted placeholder/`.env.example` ref → passes; `.env`/`.pem` path → refuse. **Interface note:** reconcile with existing pre-push secret scan (don't duplicate; this is the Edit-time layer).
- **C2 — write-lockdown PreToolUse.** Failing test: implementer scoped to `resources/views/livewire/x.blade.php` attempting write to `config/magic.php` or `app/Console/` → block; in-scope write → allow.
- **C3 — frozen-criteria check.** Failing test: editing the acceptance-criteria file after session-start SHA → fail; unchanged → pass.
- **C4 — completion Stop/SubagentStop hook.** Failing test: end turn with a declared phase lacking an evidence entry in the state file → blocked; all-evidenced → allowed.
- **C5 — MCP gate (effect ∧ target).** Failing test: `Tinker`/`RecordRule`/`browser_run_code_unsafe`/`browser_evaluate` call → deny; read-only boost tool → allow; playwright pointed at a prod origin → deny, at Herd/test.jointly.shop → allow.
- **C6 — path-fence glob→tier.** Failing test: diff touching a red glob (money/auth/migrations/config/CI) → forces review tier ≥ medium regardless of self-assessed complexity.

### Group D — Config wiring (main loop; after C exists)
- **D1 — CLAUDE.md router:** stage→skill map, rigor dial, path globs, refusal list. Test: light (loads; a routing spot-check subagent picks the right skill for 3 sample requests).
- **D2 — settings.json + SessionStart frame + UserPromptSubmit marker nudge.** Test: hooks register (use `/update-config` skill); SessionStart injects frame.

---

## PART IV — Ordering & parallelism

```
[ B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 ]  ∥  [ C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 ]   ← two parallel fan-outs (Workflow)
                    │
                    ▼
                   A1  (compose skeleton — main loop, needs B*+C* + DONE grafts)
                    │
                    ▼
                   A2  (end-to-end composition test — the integration gate)
                    │
                    ▼
                   D1, D2  (config wiring)
                    │
                    ▼
        final whole-skill review (multi-review / superpowers:requesting-code-review)
```

- **B** runs as a Haiku/Sonnet writing-skills fan-out (each graft independent — matches the pattern used twice this session).
- **C** runs worktree-isolated (hooks mutate files in parallel).
- **A, D** stay in the main loop — composition needs the whole picture; too much cross-graft context to delegate blind.
- **Rationale for NOT wrapping in SDD:** the shape is parallel-independent-authoring → single-point compose, which is Workflow + main-loop. SDD's sequential-implementer-with-code-review-between fits code tasks, not a batch of independent doc RED-GREEN loops. (Deviation from writing-plans' default SDD handoff, stated with reason.)

### HIGH — Compact hook runs too late to restore an ongoing turn

**File:** `hooks/hooks-codex.json:5`  
**Related:** `hooks/session-start-codex:48-54`

**Trigger:** A single long agent turn auto-compacts and then continues processing.

**Impact:** Codex continues the post-compaction portion of that turn without the Superpowers bootstrap or active-skill instructions. The hook runs only at the next user turn; multiple compactions can also queue duplicate injections there.

**Evidence:** Codex 0.145’s `run_pending_session_start_hooks` drains queued `SessionStartSource::Compact` events through the pending session-start path. The reproducible upstream report `openai/codex#28736` traces auto-compaction to a queued compact source drained at the next turn, including a black-box reproduction where three auto-compactions yield three delayed hook executions. The added test invokes the script directly, so it cannot detect this lifecycle-timing failure.
